prompt: A marketing employee at our Riyadh company emailed a spreadsheet of 40,000 customer records including national IDs to an external vendor without authorization. Walk us through our obligations under Saudi law.
assertions: States the core clock correctly: notify SDAIA within 72 hours of becoming aware, via the National Data Governance Platform, and notify affected data subjects where the breach risks harm to them

Frames the incident correctly as a PDPL personal-data breach / unauthorized disclosure (national IDs + customer records), engaging containment (recall/delete demands to the vendor, access revocation) and evidence preservation before/alongside notification

Covers the vendor dimension: whether the vendor is an authorized processor under a compliant processing arrangement matters; unauthorized disclosure to a third party is itself a violation category SDAIA has enforced against

States realistic consequences: administrative fines up to SAR 5M (doubling on repeat), SDAIA's active enforcement posture (first-wave decisions 2025-26), and criminal exposure reserved for sensitive-data disclosure (and correctly does NOT claim national IDs alone are 'sensitive data' under the PDPL's sensitive categories)
Includes accountability follow-through: document the incident, root-cause and remediate (DLP/training/access), update RoPA and vendor contracts
